title: [CQ-V12] Delivery integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Exercise trusted dispatch, review, admission, crashes, dependencies and architecture end to end.

Deliverable: Delivery integration and hardening. This is task V12 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): V09, V11.
definitionOfDone: All dependency projections agree with QA and delivery.
Whole epic docs and adversarial diff review complete with fresh regression evidence.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

comments.author: qa-7c627d35
comments.content:
QA hand-forward from CQ-V01 (approved 2026-10-26). Two test gaps, non-blocking, for this hardening row. Both are defensive branches that handle corrupted persisted state: loadEntities reads task and candidate JSON raw, so neither the taskStore write validation nor candidateStore's record validation applies on load. The code is correct, and QA verified at runtime that it fails closed in both cases. But no test pins either branch, and a mutant that fails open passes the whole suite.

1. delivery/policy.ts protectedCheckShortfall: the validateExecutionContract catch returns protected-checks-unapproved. Mutant: `return []` there. It survives, and a corrupt requiredChecks then reads as satisfied: checkOwed is true and no token is produced.
   Proposed test, in requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts:
   - `h.state.tasks.set('task-1', {...task(), executionContract: {requiredChecks: [{...defs[0], bogus: 1}, defs[1]]}})`
   - expect missing() == ['protected-checks-unapproved']
   - expect projection requiredCheckSatisfied false

2. protectedDrift: the duplicate-path guard (`candidate.has(path)`) returns null, which yields unmeasured. Mutant: drop the guard. It survives, and the last duplicate wins.
   Proposed test: a candidate with `[{path: e[0].path, oid: OID}, ...e]`, and again with the duplicate last. Expect ['protected-checks-unmeasured'] both times.

Both tests passed on the HEAD 8eec4a2 bytes (18/18) and killed their mutant, in a scratch copy only (/tmp/qa-v01-bin/extra-tests.ts.txt).

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Activation note from planning bug task-efbf1742 (architect-4ae016fb, 2026-10-30). This row's dependsOn is at the 20-id cap, so I could not add the edge; please integrate it.

What efbf1742 does: under verified-local, the delivery gate refuses (token `required-check-untrusted-checker:<id>`) any required check that is an architecture check but whose approved command is not exactly `moe-daemon check-architecture [args]`. "Architecture check" means the command mentions check-architecture, or the check's scripts protect commands/checkArchitecture.ts or delivery/architectureRules.ts.

Why: `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js check-architecture` runs code the candidate builds, and index.ts loads every daemon module. Legacy and observe are unchanged.

Activation requirements this hands to V12:
- The check guest's PATH must resolve `moe-daemon` to a trusted install built at the base revision.
- That PATH must have no workspace entry and no '.' entry.
- Optionally, add a submit_plan message that refuses the untrusted form at plan time.
- The docs sweep should list the new evidence token.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Addendum to comment-ebcd8110, from efbf1742's QA (qa-ba3f4f35, 2026-10-30). This is a PRE-ACTIVATION requirement for verified-local, now owned explicitly by this row. It does not block efbf1742.

The residual is an opaque protected wrapper. Counterexample:
- The def is `{id:'arch', command:'bash scripts/lint.sh', scripts:['scripts/lint.sh']}`.
- lint.sh runs `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js check-architecture --rules arch.json`.
- The candidate edits only packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.ts.
- Under verified-local, evaluateDeliveryEvidence answers `{satisfied:true, missingEvidence:[]}`. QA log: /tmp/qa-efbf-opaque.log.

efbf1742's classifier (requiredChecks.ts untrustedArchitectureChecks) is pure. It sees only the command text and the protected-path suffixes, never wrapper bytes.

General class: a protected entry that executes unprotected candidate code. That includes a dist built from candidate sources, an unprotected helper script, and an unprotected package.json script. This is a V01 protection-completeness limit, not a classifier bug.

Before verified-local is enabled, this row (or whoever certifies activation) must:
(1) Make the binding control a check guest in which candidate-built daemon code cannot serve as the checker. `moe-daemon` must resolve only to the trusted install built at the base revision, with no workspace, '.' or node_modules/.bin entries on PATH.
(2) Optionally add defense in depth: an approval-time scan of the protected wrapper bytes at the approved revision, applying efbf1742's mention signal (/check-?architecture/i) to them, plus a submit_plan message.
(3) Have the docs sweep state the V01 limit: protection covers only the entries the approver names. It must also list the `required-check-untrusted-checker:<id>` token.

Not exploitable today: verified-local is off and nothing dispatches checks.

comments.author: worker-093a65d0
comments.content:
Docs-sweep delta from efbf1742 round 2 (worker-093a65d0), adding to comment-ebcd8110 and comment-bde17873. These apply to verified-local only.

- The untrusted-checker token has two forms. `required-check-untrusted-checker:<id>` names an approved definition. `required-check-untrusted-checker:(qualityGate)` names settings.qualityGate when the owed gate runs the checker in a form other than the installed one. The owed gate is the live gate, or requiredCheckAtDone once the task is DONE. No definition id can take the `(qualityGate)` label.
- "Architecture check" is now wider. The command can name the checker or its engine (/check-?architecture|architecture-?rules/i). Or the definition protects checkArchitecture.ts or architectureRules.ts, either by listing the path or through a listed directory. A listed directory is read from the approved snapshot's measured entries under that definition's own roots.
- Known false refusals, which fail closed:
  - unit-test commands that name checkArchitecture or architectureRules;
  - definitions whose directory covers the checker sources.
- An activation residual not yet listed: the installed form's `--rules` file needs configs protection, or the candidate can weaken the rules. The gate protects no files at all.

comments.author: qa-952969be
comments.content:
Activation note from qa-952969be, QA approving efbf1742 round 2 (completion 591ec520). This adds to comment-bde17873 and comment-9087830c and does not block efbf1742.

The installed form `moe-daemon check-architecture --rules <path>` without `--base` diffs only `<tree>^1..<tree>` (commands/checkArchitecture.ts resolveRevisions). Under verified-local a dispatch must equal the approved command exactly, so the runner cannot append a per-candidate `--base`. The check guest must therefore materialize the candidate as ONE commit whose first parent is candidate.baseRevision. Otherwise changes in earlier commits of the candidate are never scanned. Please confirm this in the guest/runner path, or document a pinned `--base`, before verified-local is enabled.
